text:
Alex Chen: quick flag — noticed a host-side p99 regression after the kernel-selector change last night. p99 for short seqs went 82ms -> 98ms. looks like unpack/flush path is hotter.
Maria Gomez: ugh. which kernel roll? the one that prefers wide-matrix kernels for sequence < 64?
Alex Chen: yeah, KERNEL_V2 that biases toward larger GEMM for improved throughput. it seems to increase preproc contention — tokenization + small writev cost.
Samir Patel: can you drop a perf snippet? also did kv-cache hitrate change?
Alex Chen: paste of `perf top` (trimmed):
```
  34.2%  libredwood.so  parse_frame
  18.7%  libredwood.so  writev_flush
  12.3%  libc.so        memcpy
  8.1%   tokenizer.so   tokenize_short
  6.9%   libredwood.so  kv_cache_lookup
```
Jordan Lee: interesting — parse_frame + writev_flush dominating. that matches increased syscall rate from smaller streaming chunks. did the streaming-chunker config change?
Alex Chen: yes — autoslicer now emits 128B chunks for small-client traffic (aim was reduce latency). but that raised # of writev calls.
Maria Gomez: kv_cache_lookup is nontrivial here. any evictions?
Alex Chen: eviction rate spiked ~3x on the perf run; hot-shard contention increased too. suspect the kernel swap changed latency distribution (CPU stalls) so background kv maintenance couldn't keep up.
Samir Patel: hypothesis: kernel selection increased CPU compute time per batch, so the host preproc (tokenize+frame) queues up and sends more frequent tiny writev bursts when KV misses occur. two levers: 1) increase streaming chunk to 512B for small seqs; 2) bias kernel selector back for tiny batches.
Maria Gomez: can we try a quick A/B? revert kernel to KERNEL_V1 but keep new batching heuristics. also run a run with larger chunk size (512B) to measure writev tail.
Alex Chen: started canary deploys: KERNEL=V1 on canary and CHUNK_SIZE=512 for 10% traffic. perf-bot reported diff: host-preproc p50 unchanged, p99 -7ms on canary.
perf-bot: nightly-diff: host-unpack-flush: p99 -7ms (canary), kv-evictions -62% (canary) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Jordan Lee: good signal. but we need to understand why KERNEL_V2 triggers more evictions. maybe KERNEL_V2 changes batch packing so KV hits across requests are less coalesced.
Samir Patel: looking at batching heuristics — V2 groups by model size then kernel hint. that can scatter requests across host shards. if shard affinity drops, kv locality suffers.
Maria Gomez: pointers: 1) add batching affinity window (group by host-shard id before kernel choice), 2) make KV lookup async-friendly (poll vs blocking), 3) coalesce writev for consecutive small chunks into a single batched write when tail latency allows.
Alex Chen: logged experiment: set affinity_window_ms=30 and enable writev_coalesce=true for canary. also instrumenting: add counters for writev_coalesce_hits, kv_eviction_rate, kernel_choice_distribution.
Samir Patel: small config snippet for the canary we used:
```
  KERNEL_SELECTOR=V1
  STREAM_CHUNK_BYTES=512
  BATCH_AFFINITY_MS=30
  WRITEV_COALESCE=true
```
Maria Gomez: after 30m of canary: writev_syscalls down 48%, kv_evictions down 58%, p99 down 9ms. looks promising.
Jordan Lee: next: validate end-to-end for long seq traffic (we don't want regression there). also run a microbench to verify CPU utilization per kernel variant.
Alex Chen: ran microbench (short seq): V1 CPU per-token 0.9us, V2 0.85us but external preproc overhead pushes end-to-end higher on V2 due to increased syscalls and kv churn.
Samir Patel: conclusion: kernel-level perf gain is real but host-side systems (tokenizer, chunker, kv) must adapt — otherwise global tail gets worse. plan: keep KERNEL_V1 default, iterate on V2 to respect host affinity and writev coalescing.
Maria Gomez: can we gate V2 behind a runtime flag that checks kv_hitrate and writev_rate? only flip when safe.
Alex Chen: yes, added rollout rule: only enable V2 when host.writev_rate < 300/s and kv.hitrate > 0.85. will run staged rollout next week.
Jordan Lee: thanks — please add postmortem notes to the perf board and link traces.
Alex Chen: will do, uploading perf traces + flamegraphs to the ticket. TL;DR: kernel selection changed compute distribution -> amplified host-side small-write + kv-thrashing -> tail regression. fix = affinity + coalesce + guarded rollout. :thumbsup:
